bug_description.original: An uninitialized read occurs in decompress_smooth_data() when cinfo->output_iMCU_row is greater than cinfo->master->last_good_iMCU_row and cinfo->input_scan_number equals 1, causing the function to read from prev_coef_bits_latch[], which is uninitialized.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 239-byte JPEG parses as a progressive frame and reaches a first SOS with scan parameters `Ss=0, Se=0, Ah=0, Al=1`, so libjpeg-turbo enters the progressive Huffman/block-smoothing path with `input_scan_number == 1`. `jinit_phuff_decoder()` allocates `cinfo->coef_bits` for two planes per component but initializes only the current-scan plane to `-1`; `start_pass_phuff_decoder()` then updates only the current DC status for scan 1 and still skips the guarded previous-plane copy. Later `smoothing_ok()` allocates `coef->coef_bits_latch`, splits it into current- and previous-scan halves, and for coefficients 1..9 writes `prev_coef_bits_latch[coefi]` only when `input_scan_number > 1`. On the first scan those previous-scan latch slots remain uninitialized small-pool bytes. `start_output_pass()` still selects `decompress_smooth_data()`, and when output later advances beyond `last_good_iMCU_row`, `decompress_smooth_data()` switches `coef_bits` to that previous-scan latch half and evaluates `coef_bits[1]..coef_bits[9]` in the `change_dc` predicate. MemorySanitizer reports the resulting use-of-uninitialized-value at `jdcoefct.c:519`.

source.code: cinfo->progressive_mode = is_prog; ... INPUT_BYTE(cinfo, cinfo->num_components, return FALSE);
source.description: First project parser step on the vulnerable path: the SOF parser materializes the staged frame as progressive and records the component count, which later drives progressive Huffman setup and the size/layout of the smoothing latches.
source.value_from: The staged 239-byte PoC contains the progressive SOF2 marker `ff c2` starting at byte offset `0x73`; the SOF payload that follows encodes `num_components = 1`. When `jpeg_read_header()` dispatches to `get_sof(cinfo, TRUE, FALSE)`, libjpeg-turbo records that attacker-controlled frame state in `cinfo` before any smoothing logic runs.

tainted_value_origin.description: The uninitialized values later read at the sink are the previous-scan latch integers `prev_coef_bits_latch[1..9]` in the second half of `coef->coef_bits_latch`. They originate in newly allocated small-pool storage that is not zeroed before first use.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `decompress_smooth_data()` computes `change_dc` by comparing the first nine AC-status entries through `coef_bits`; when `coef_bits` points at the previous-scan latch half, those integer reads touch never-written slots from `prev_coef_bits_latch`.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value in decompress_smooth_data() at /src/libjpeg-turbo/jdcoefct.c:519:26`.

root_cause.description: First-scan latch-initialization bug: `smoothing_ok()` only writes the previous-scan latch entries when `input_scan_number > 1`, even though later output code may still read those entries as the previous scan's coefficient state.
root_cause.note: On scan 1 the branch is skipped, so `prev_coef_bits_latch[1..9]` stay uninitialized in the freshly allocated pool object. The fix adds the missing first-scan initializer `prev_coef_bits_latch[coefi] = -1;` in the `else` arm.

parser_admitted.condition: The staged JPEG reaches its first SOS, loads scan parameters `Ss=0, Se=0, Ah=0, Al=1`, and increments `input_scan_number` to 1, establishing the exact first-scan state later consumed by `start_pass_phuff_decoder()` and `smoothing_ok()`.

coarse_trace.summary: The `dct_fuzzer` witness passes the staged JPEG bytes to libjpeg-turbo with `jpeg_buffer_src()`, then drives `jpeg_read_header()`, `jpeg_start_decompress()`, and repeated `jpeg_read_scanlines()` calls.
SOF2 parsing records progressive-frame state and component count from the PoC, which makes the progressive Huffman and block-smoothing paths eligible.
The first SOS records scan parameters `Ss=0, Se=0, Ah=0, Al=1` and increments `input_scan_number` to 1, establishing the exact first-scan state that drives the later missing previous-scan writes.
The progressive decoder allocates `cinfo->coef_bits` for two planes per component but initializes only the current-scan plane to `-1`, leaving the current AC status slots 1..9 marked unknown.
For the first DC scan, `start_pass_phuff_decoder()` writes the current DC status `coef_bit_ptr[0] = Al = 1` and, because `input_scan_number == 1`, skips copying any previous-scan status.
Block smoothing allocates a separate latch buffer and, on scan 1, leaves `prev_coef_bits_latch[1..9]` unwritten while still returning true because the current AC status entries remain nonzero (`-1`).
Because block smoothing remains enabled and `smoothing_ok()` succeeded, the output controller installs `decompress_smooth_data()`.
When output advances beyond `last_good_iMCU_row`, the smooth path switches to the previous-scan latch half and reads those uninitialized integers in the `change_dc` predicate at line 519.

fine_trace.code: cinfo->progressive_mode = is_prog; ... INPUT_BYTE(cinfo, cinfo->num_components, return FALSE);
fine_trace.note: Parsing the SOF2 header marks the staged JPEG as progressive and reads `num_components = 1` into the decompressor. Those fields later control progressive Huffman setup and the size/layout of the coefficient-state buffers.

The first SOS in the staged JPEG materializes scan parameters `Ss=0, Se=0, Ah=0, Al=1` and increments `input_scan_number` from 0 to 1. That first-scan state is later consumed both by `start_pass_phuff_decoder()` and by the vulnerable latch initialization.

The progressive decoder allocates `cinfo->coef_bits` large enough for a current and previous plane per component, but this loop initializes only the first `num_components * DCTSIZE2` ints. On the witness that means the current AC status slots 1..9 start as `-1`.

For the witness's first DC scan, the second loop writes `coef_bit_ptr[0] = Al = 1`. Because `input_scan_number == 1`, the guarded copy into `prev_coef_bit_ptr` does not execute, and current AC status entries 1..9 remain the `-1` values from step 3.

When block smoothing is evaluated, libjpeg-turbo allocates a separate latch buffer and splits it into current-scan and previous-scan halves. `alloc_small()` uses small-pool storage without clearing it first, so the `prev_coef_bits_latch` integers are indeterminate until explicitly written.

fine_trace.code: if (coef_bits[0] < 0) return FALSE; ... if (cinfo->input_scan_number > 1) prev_coef_bits_latch[coefi] = prev_coef_bits[coefi]; coef_bits_latch[coefi] = coef_bits[coefi]; if (coef_bits[coefi] != 0) smoothing_useful = TRUE;
fine_trace.note: Because step 4 made `coef_bits[0] = 1`, the DC-known guard passes. For coefficients 1..9 on scan 1, the only store into `prev_coef_bits_latch[coefi]` is skipped, leaving those slots in the allocator state from step 5. The current-scan latch is still written from `coef_bits[coefi] == -1`, and `-1 != 0` makes `smoothing_useful` true, so `smoothing_ok()` can return true despite the missing previous-latch initialization.

With `do_block_smoothing` defaulting to TRUE and step 6 leaving `smoothing_useful` true, the output pass installs `decompress_smooth_data()` as the decompression routine. That selection is required for the later read from the previous-scan latch half.

fine_trace.code: if (cinfo->output_iMCU_row > cinfo->master->last_good_iMCU_row) coef_bits = coef->coef_bits_latch + ((ci + cinfo->num_components) * SAVED_COEFS);
fine_trace.note: On a row beyond `last_good_iMCU_row`, the smooth-output path retargets `coef_bits` to the second half of `coef->coef_bits_latch`, i.e. the previous-scan latch. Because step 6 fully wrote the current half but not the previous half, the saved MSAN read at line 519 implies this arm executed.

fine_trace.code: change_dc = coef_bits[1] == -1 && coef_bits[2] == -1 && coef_bits[3] == -1 && coef_bits[4] == -1 && coef_bits[5] == -1 && coef_bits[6] == -1 && coef_bits[7] == -1 && coef_bits[8] == -1 && coef_bits[9] == -1;
fine_trace.note: The `change_dc` predicate reads the first nine AC-status integers through the pointer chosen in step 8. Because that pointer now names `prev_coef_bits_latch` and step 6 never initialized those integers on scan 1, the comparisons consume uninitialized memory and the run crashes at `jdcoefct.c:519:26`.

allocation_context.note: The MSAN origin stack is `malloc -> alloc_small -> get_sof` at the first `comp_info` allocation. `coef->coef_bits_latch` is later carved from the same uninitialized small-object pool, so the report names the earlier slab allocation rather than the exact latch allocation site.

format.name: malformed progressive JPEG
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 239-byte JPEG `poc` (sha256 `86501d1aa8748f5e85c8e9a8858377f705e56e9b07821c9510e2fb417fdf57c0`). The witness contains a progressive SOF2 and a first SOS with `Ss=0, Se=0, Ah=0, Al=1`, so libjpeg-turbo enters progressive Huffman/block-smoothing mode with `input_scan_number == 1`. In the saved MSAN crash, `smoothing_ok()` leaves `prev_coef_bits_latch[1..9]` unwritten on that first scan, and `decompress_smooth_data()` later reaches a row where `output_iMCU_row > last_good_iMCU_row`, switches to the previous-scan latch half, and reads those same slots in `change_dc`. This contract is witness-specific; the staged artifacts do not establish a broader malformed-JPEG family beyond inputs that recreate that same first-scan previous-latch read.
